messages:
ravi: heads-up — canary for rollout A (deploy abc1234) is showing a ~35% token/sec drop since the merge of PR #4321. throughput and tail latency both worse. suspect CTB/scheduler interaction. :eyes:
perfbot: CI perf job failed: https://ci.redwood/987 — baseline 215k tok/s -> current 140k tok/s :warning:
eva: any flamegraphs or kernel-selection logs? is this a kernel fallback or batching heuristic change?
dan: attaching quick snapshot from the profiler run on the canary box:
```
Profile summary:
- total_tokens: 1.2M
- avg_tok_per_sec: 142k
- kernel_time: 420s
- memcpy_time: 210s (was 60s pre-merge)
- kernel_selected: attention_generic (used to be fused_attention_fast)
- ctb_drain_waits: spike from 120->980
```
maya: bisect narrowed it down to commit def5678 (author: infra-batching) — that commit changed the prefetch/poll interval and a small refactor in kernel hint propagation. git-bisect output below:
```
$ git bisect visualize
first bad commit: def5678
good:  abc9999
bad:   def5678
PR:   4321
```
liam: if kernel hints aren't propagating the runtime falls back to generic attention which is memory-bound on our GPU, explains memcpy spike. did the refactor drop the hint flag on the CTB path?
eva: can you paste the scheduler log lines where kernel_hint is set? or search for `kernel_hint=` in the canary logs.
dan: found it — kernel_hint present in the serve path but missing on the batched request entry for continuous-batcher. snippet:
```
[2025-11-22T14:12:03Z] serve: kernel_hint=fused_attention_fast
[2025-11-22T14:12:03Z] ctb: enqueue req_id=42 (kernel_hint=)
```
ravi: that matches. also seeing KV cache hitrate drop during the same window (was ~92% -> ~66%). not sure if it's related but it increases cold prefixes causing more memcpy.
maya: here's a quick repro command for local perf runs — reproduces the token/sec drop in ~30s:
```bash
python infra/bench/run_sched_repro.py --model redwood/llama-13b --seq 2048 --concurrency 16 --enable-ctb --warmup 200
```
liam: suggested mitigation: re-apply kernel_hint before enqueue in CTB path. quick patch already sketched, will open PR if we need to revert instead.
perfbot: regression test link: https://perf.redwood/job/ctb-throughput-compare/44 (compare run/43)
deploy-bot: holding rollout A (canary) due to perf regression. rollback recommended: PR #4325 (revert of 4321) is drafted.
eva: also check the prefetch interval change — if CTB is polling too often it can fragment batches, causing more small batches and poorly utilized kernels. add metric: batch_size_distribution and inter-arrival histogram.
dan: flamegraph attached (pasted small ascii):
```
fused_attention_fast         |████████████████████
attention_generic           |██████████████████████████████████
memcpy                      |████████████████████████
ctb_enqueue_wait            |██████████████
```
maya: I'm going to push a minimal fix to restore kernel_hint propagation in CTB path. if tests pass we'll roll forward; otherwise we'll merge revert PR #4325.
ravi: ok pls do both: PR for fix + CI run. holding rollout until we confirm <10% perf delta. tagging @eva for verification and @liam for kernel change review. :hammer:
liam: quick patch LGTM locally, but want one more perf run under the real canary workload.
perfbot: nightly perf job scheduled with the fix applied — will post results here once complete.
ravi: thanks everyone. holding canary and marking this as a rollout blocker for the hour. label: perf/blocker. :thumbsup:
